title: What is a Recurrent Neural Network? The LSTM Architecture
description: How loop-back connections give RNNs memory across time steps, and how LSTM's gates preserve long-term dependencies while taming vanishing gradients.
content:
**Recurrent Neural Network (RNN)** is a type of neural network designed to handle sequential data by maintaining internal memory. Unlike feedforward neural networks, where data is processed in one direction, RNNs have loop-back connections that help keep previous context.

Tasks where time dependencies are crucial:
• Natural language processing (NLP)
• Speech recognition
• Time series analysis

How an RNN processes a sequence:
• Data is processed unit by unit, one at each time step.
• Previous data is retained in the hidden layers.
• At each time step, the model combines the input and the hidden state to produce an output and update the hidden state, so the previous context is considered.

The primary challenge:
• The vanishing gradient problem - gradients shrink as they are propagated back through many time steps.
• Conversely, gradients can also explode.

**Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM)** is a type of RNN architecture designed to overcome vanishing and exploding gradient problems and capture long-term dependencies in sequential data. LSTM has a more complex internal structure containing:
• Forget gates - decide what information to discard from the previous cell state.
• Input gates - determine which new information is added to the cell state.
• Cell state update - combines the retained past information and the new candidate to update the cell's memory.
• Output gates - determine what the next hidden state (and possibly the output) should be by regulating what information from the cell state is exposed to the next time step.

This allows LSTM to capture and retain information over longer periods or sequences and helps mitigate the vanishing gradient problem.
